title: Redefining Test-and-Treat to assure chronic hepatitis C elimination in individuals-at-risk through point-of-care treatment as part of ‘Fast Track City’ initiative in Berlin
summary:
Background:
New highly effective medicines now make it possible to cure chronic hepatitis C infection in most cases. The World Health Organization has therefore set the goal of largely eliminating this infection worldwide by the year 2030. Despite major progress, significant challenges remain, particularly among people at increased risk who rarely access the regular health care system. This includes people who inject drugs as well as individuals without stable housing or without regular access to medical care. Many people in these groups are tested but do not start treatment or drop out of care early. Low-threshold drug support facilities, which combine medical, social, and preventive services, could play an important role in closing this gap.

Research question:
The study investigates which care strategy improves access to treatment and treatment success among people at increased risk. It compares treatment provided directly in low-threshold drug support facilities with the usual approach, in which individuals with a positive test are referred to general practitioners or hospital-based services.

Methods:
People from risk groups will be tested for hepatitis C in drug support facilities. In one group, treatment will be started directly at the facility. In the comparison group, participants will be referred to physicians or specialized medical services for further assessment and treatment. The study will then examine how many individuals start treatment and how many successfully complete it. In addition, outcomes such as treatment success several weeks after the end of therapy, attendance at follow-up visits, regular intake of medication, and the proportion of participants who are lost to follow-up will be assessed. The study will also collect data on the frequency of hepatitis C infection in particularly affected areas of Berlin in order to better plan future prevention and elimination strategies.

interventions.name: Study arm 1 reflects the conventional pathway of hepatitis C diagnosis and treatment within the routine healthcare system. Individuals from at-risk populations are screened in cooperating facilities. In the case of a positive HCV RNA test, participants are referred to specialized hepatology practice

Study arm 2 comprises a low-threshold test-and-treat approach with immediate initiation of therapy in cooperating addiction care facilities. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Subjects with the following characteristics:
-	Positive test for HCV RNA in PCR
-	Capable of written informed consent for study participation.

The inclusion into the study is possible without current access to health care insurance coverage, as the study population usually has either limited or no access to health insurance coverage and would (following standard-of-care) otherwise not be able to receive treatment for HCV.
Exclusion criteria:
Subjects with the following characteristics:
- Younger than 18 years of age
- Incapable of written informed consent
- In a legal guardianship relationship (according to §1814 BGB)
- With (high-grade) evidence of decompensated cirrhosis as assessed by the health care professional
- Pregnancy
- Currently on medication that is contraindicated for coadministration with GLE/PIB as per German drug label

The exclusion criteria do not consider a participant’s insurance status. A previously diagnosed and successfully treated hepatitis C virus infection is likewise not an exclusion criterion. Ongoing intravenous drug use and opioid substitution therapy are also not grounds for exclusion.
Participants who, at screening, show evidence of decompensated liver cirrhosis - such as hepatic encephalopathy, active infection, ascites or hydropic decompensation, markedly reduced urine output indicative of severe renal dysfunction, or recent variceal or non-variceal bleeding - should be referred to a hepatology-specialized healthcare facility for further management.
